questions.q: Where do you go to configure scheduled refresh for a semantic model?
options: Open the semantic model's details page in its workspace, then select Refresh → Schedule refresh
It can only be configured from within Power BI Desktop
It's configured from the workspace's general settings, unrelated to any specific semantic model
There's no way to schedule refresh — every refresh must be manual
questions.explain: Every scheduled-refresh setting — frequency, time slots, gateway, credentials — lives behind the semantic model's own Refresh → Schedule refresh menu.

questions.q: What does the 'Data source credentials' section show when using a standard (enterprise) gateway instead of personal mode?
options: It's grayed out, since credentials are defined centrally by the gateway administrator, not the individual user
It requires re-entering credentials before every single refresh
It's identical to the personal-mode experience in every way
It only appears for DirectQuery semantic models
questions.explain: With a standard gateway, the gateway admin has already configured the data source credentials centrally — there's nothing for the individual user to enter.

questions.q: What happens after two months with no user viewing any report or dashboard built on a semantic model?
options: Power BI automatically pauses the scheduled refresh, emails the owner, and marks the schedule as Disabled
Nothing changes — refresh continues indefinitely regardless of usage
The semantic model is automatically deleted
The refresh frequency automatically doubles to compensate
questions.explain: This is the inactivity pause: two months with zero views (through any report, dashboard, or app) triggers an automatic pause, an email to the owner, and a Disabled schedule status.

questions.q: How do you resume a scheduled refresh that was paused due to inactivity?
options: Open any report or dashboard that uses the semantic model, then re-enable the schedule if needed
It's impossible to resume — a new semantic model must be created from scratch
Wait exactly 24 hours and it resumes automatically with no action needed
Contact Microsoft support directly, since this can't be self-resolved
questions.explain: Simply viewing any report or dashboard connected to the semantic model resets the inactivity counter; you may then need to re-enable the schedule if it doesn't restart on its own.

questions.q: Roughly when does Power BI target starting a scheduled refresh relative to its scheduled time slot?
options: Within 15 minutes of the slot, though delays up to an hour can occur, and it can start as early as 5 minutes before
Exactly at the scheduled second, with zero tolerance
Only ever at midnight, regardless of the configured slot
Refresh timing is entirely random and unrelated to the configured slot
questions.explain: Power BI aims for a 15-minute window after the scheduled slot, with a possible delay up to an hour if resources aren't immediately available, and can begin as early as 5 minutes before.
